predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Saxony
predecessors.text: the archbishopric with the city of Bremen

ledger.x: 1180: Barbarossa breaks up the Duchy of Saxony and 'the Ascanians secured the see for Siegfried of Anhalt'; 'part of the diocesan territory' was upgraded to the Prince-Archbishopric.
1186: the Gelnhausen Privilege 'recognized Bremen as a political body'; the city was 'de facto (since 1186) and de jure (since 1646) not part of the prince-archbishopric'.
Christmas 1229: the first battle with the Stedingers.
1525: the Treaty of Stade, which ended the election of consuls.
1525: 'In 1525 the Wursten Consuls had to conclude the Treaty of Stade,' which incorporated Wursten into the prince-archbishopric.
Summer 1627: Tilly invades and captures the southern parts; in 1628 he besieged Stade and on 5 May 1628 granted safe-conduct, so 'the whole archbishopric was in his hands'.
10 May 1632: the Leaguist forces are granted safe-conduct and leave Stade.
1643-1645: during the Torstenson War the Swedes seize de facto rule of the archbishopric; on 13 August 1645 the Second Peace of Brömsebro cedes the prince-bishoprics to Sweden.
15 May 1648: the infobox date of secularisation.
15 May 1648: secularised as the hereditary Duchy of Bremen.

wars.name: Stedinger Crusades
wars.outcome: The Stedingers won at Christmas 1229 and repelled the crusaders on 6 July 1233; a second crusade under Henry I of Brabant crushed them at Altenesch in 1234.

wars.name: Subjection of Wursten
wars.outcome: Christopher the Spendthrift's troops defeated the Wursten Frisians at Mulsum on 9 August 1524 and the Treaty of Stade of 1525 incorporated Wursten.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War in the archbishopric
wars.outcome: Christian IV of Denmark stationed troops in Stade in 1619-1620; Tilly beat him at Lutter on 27 August 1626, invaded in 1627 and held the whole archbishopric after 5 May 1628; the Edict of Restitution of 6 March 1629 covered Bremen and Verden; the Treaty of…

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: The Swedes seized de facto rule of the archbishopric in 1643-1645 and the Second Peace of Brömsebro of 13 August 1645 ceded the prince-bishoprics to Sweden.

certainty.note: The page names no border; the territory is a circle between the Weser and the Elbe and smaller circles for Stedingen, Bremen and Wursten.
